chunk_findings.detail: `_is_ghost` computes silence from `last_event` only (`now - last`), while `_free` immediately computes `quiet` from `max(last_event, heartbeat)` and `_heard_from` treats a heartbeat as proof the lane is heard from. Given `[lanes].ghost_after_s=7200`, `[lanes].idle_s=900`, `now=100000.0`, a free lane with `last_event=92000.0` (8000 s old), `heartbeat=99500.0` (500 s old), and any ready work: `_free` sets `quiet=500.0`, so `_heard_from` would be true, but `_is_ghost` returns true because `8000.0 >= 7200`, so `_free` returns `Lane(state=S.GONE, ...)`. The lane is hidden/counted as gone despite a fresh heartbeat, preventing it from being shown as idle-ready or used by advise.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/ledger.py:_is_ghost

chunk_findings.detail: The footer text can tell the user that `--all` will list lanes even when `[output].allow_full` is false. `_row_cap` sets `refused = show_all` when `allow_full` is false, so in the default view (`show_all=False`) `refused` is always false; the `more` note then prints “everything: `ddflow lanes --all` …”. The `gone` note always prints “`ddflow lanes --all` … lists them” without checking `allow_full` at all. Given `[output] allow_full=false`, `max_rows=10`, and 20 non-gone lanes (or 100 gone lanes), `select_roster` emits a footer promising that `--all` lists everything, but calling `select_roster(..., show_all=True)` still applies the 10-row cap and omits lanes. This contradicts the intended behavior that `--all` lifts the cap only when `allow_full` is true.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/roster.py:72-79

chunk_findings.detail: The footer promises that `ddflow lanes --all` will list omitted lanes even when `[output].allow_full = false` prevents `--all` from lifting the row cap. `_row_cap` sets `refused = show_all`, so for the default table (`show_all=False`) `refused` is false even though `--all` would be refused; the “more” footer then says “everything: `ddflow lanes --all`”. The “gone” footer also unconditionally says `--all` lists the gone lanes. Concrete: with `cfg.output.allow_full=False`, `cfg.output.max_rows=10`, and 15 non-gone lanes, `select_roster(..., show_all=False)` returns a footer saying the 5 omitted lanes can be seen with `--all`, but `select_roster(..., show_all=True)` with the same config returns only 10 shown and 5 more, so `--all` does not list everything. The same mismatch applies to gone lanes: with 100 gone lanes and 10 non-gone lanes, the default footer says `--all` lists the 100 gone lanes, while `--all` keeps the 10 non-gone lanes first and cuts all gone lanes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/roster.py:select_roster/_row_cap

chunk_findings.detail: The new `--all` help line says `ddflow lanes --all` lists every lane “past the `[output].max_rows` row cap”, but the same section says the table is cut at `[output].max_rows` with an `N more` footer, and the new upgrade record says the table is cut at `[output].max_rows`. Given `[output].max_rows = 10` and 100 lanes, the help promises that `ddflow lanes --all` / `ddflow_lanes all=true` prints all 100 rows; if the implementation follows that, the newly added row cap can be bypassed and the command can still emit the full 147-line roster, defeating the stated bounded-output goal. If the implementation follows the cap, the new `--all` documentation is false.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/lanes.md:8

data.summary: The plain ddflow on PATH runs the primary checkout's code; when another lane has an uncommitted, half-written edit there (observed: ddflow/services/leases/lifecycle.py line 464, a docstring fused with the next statement) every ddflow command from any lane aborts with a SyntaxError traceback, including claim/update. Repro: edit a module under the primary's ddflow/ to be unparsable, run ddflow update <item> from another lane. Expected: lanes keep working from their own tree or the CLI names the broken file and the worktree wrapper.
data.title: ddflow CLI aborts with a SyntaxError while another lane edits the primary checkout

data.summary: In a task worktree, the advice to format before commit (ruff format ddflow) rewrites every unformatted file of the tree, including ddflow/api/gates/_run.py leased by another lane (KL-kill-cause); the lease hook only refused at commit time, after git add -A had staged it. The complexity/format advice should name a scoped command (ruff format <the item's globs>) and the standards tooling should not format outside the item's globs. Observed 2026-11-13 on WF-lanes-roster-cap; reverted by git restore.
data.title: A whole-tree ruff format in a worktree rewrites files held by other lanes and the commit is only stopped at git add time
